data.narrative:
Hybron is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Brennan Lieu and Aaron Guo that has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 9 private companies (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the narrow peer set limits the applicability of certain methods.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach, using total capital raised ($30M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $75M. The Peer-Median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables within the robotics and manufacturing sector—while 10 same-sector peers exist, none satisfied the narrow filter criteria (≥3 datapoints required).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $64M (low) to $86M (high), with a median of $75M. This range reflects the step-up methodology applied to the $30M raised baseline. Key uncertainties include the lack of robust peer-group validation; a more granular comparable set at the Seed-A boundary would strengthen conviction. Sector maturity, capital intensity, and the absence of meaningful revenue or unit economics data also limit precision. Additional data on Seed-A progressions in the robotics sector or revenue metrics would refine this estimate.
